nodes.label: Why the PHP harness suite was committed
nodes.rationale: Committed as three standalone CLI PHP harness suites (rewriter-test, convert-restore-e2e, bulk-e2e; 150 assertions total) because an earlier set of assertions lived only in a session scratchpad and was lost when that session ended, taking 143 assertions of regression cover with it. Standalone scripts rather than PHPUnit so they can run directly against real WordPress with a single php invocation.
nodes.norm_label: why the php harness suite was committed

nodes.label: Why every WordPress-backed harness checks siteurl first
nodes.rationale: harness_require_site() refuses to run unless get_option('siteurl') equals https://cb-test.local, because Local Sites names every database 'local' and distinguishes sites only by MySQL socket. Pairing the wrong socket with a site's files silently points the harness at a different site's database while everything appears to work, and has already produced two confidently-reported findings that were fiction plus a run that deleted 54 real user backups.
nodes.norm_label: why every wordpress-backed harness checks siteurl first

nodes.label: Why harness cleanup never globs the backup directory
nodes.rationale: harness_cleanup() resolves and deletes backups only through the manifest recorded on each attachment's own OptimizationLog row, never by scanning the backup directory, because a previous harness's cleanup used glob(BackupManager::root().'/@*/@*/@*') and destroyed 54 real user backups covering 228 original files.
nodes.norm_label: why harness cleanup never globs the backup directory

nodes.label: Why web-runner.php exists
nodes.rationale: web-runner.php lets the harness suites run under the site's web PHP (php-fpm) instead of CLI PHP, because CLI PHP on this environment lacks the Imagick extension while the site's web PHP has it. A CLI-only run would silently fall back to cwebp regardless of the engine requested, which is how the cwebp portrait-rotation bug (issue I-2) reached production without being caught.

nodes.label: App root component (Masthead, HeroStats, Tabs shell)
nodes.norm_label: app root component (masthead, herostats, tabs shell)

nodes.label: Toasts replace notices for transient feedback
nodes.rationale: A save confirmed or an action finished is true for a moment and needs no response, so it should not push the page around or leave the operator something to dismiss. Errors stay as persistent Notices because they describe something still wrong until acted upon. Built with no @wordpress/components or toast library; the provider owns the timers so callers never handle cleanup.
nodes.norm_label: toasts replace notices for transient feedback

nodes.label: Reconcile running state with server on mount
nodes.rationale: Previously the mount effect set progress but never `running`, so a run already in progress rendered the Start button as available; clicking it reset a live run, producing 'bulk already running' from a button that looked idle. The server is now treated as the authority on whether a run is active.
nodes.norm_label: reconcile running state with server on mount

nodes.label: Poll bulk/status independently of the local batch loop
nodes.rationale: Cron or another browser tab can now advance a run, so this tab must see progress it did not itself cause. Without independent polling, the displayed numbers only moved when this tab's own foreground loop happened to be driving.
nodes.norm_label: poll bulk/status independently of the local batch loop

nodes.label: Percent read from server rather than computed client-side
nodes.rationale: Two clients each computing their own percentage over different snapshots produced disagreeing figures mid-run, so the server now computes and returns `percent` directly.
nodes.norm_label: percent read from server rather than computed client-side

nodes.label: bulk-locked response treated as hand-off, not an error
nodes.rationale: A `bulk-locked` error code means cron or another tab already claimed this batch, which is ordinary now that multiple drivers exist. The foreground loop returns silently and lets the independent status poll keep the display current instead of surfacing an error for expected contention.
nodes.norm_label: bulk-locked response treated as hand-off, not an error

nodes.label: Start button becomes Resume for a resumable run
nodes.rationale: Resuming continues work the operator already agreed to, so it skips the confirm() warning that a genuinely new run still requires.
nodes.norm_label: start button becomes resume for a resumable run

nodes.label: Stalled warning explains WP-Cron only fires on site traffic
nodes.rationale: A run can be active with no recent completed batch because background processing relies on WP-Cron, which only runs when someone visits the site; the warning tells the operator to keep the page open or set up a real system cron.
nodes.norm_label: stalled warning explains wp-cron only fires on site traffic

nodes.label: MySQL socket pinned to aRpCXvFUz to avoid cross-site pairing
nodes.rationale: Local names every database `local` and distinguishes sites only by the MySQL socket, so the wrong socket would silently pair this plugin's files with another site's database while appearing to work. The socket is pinned rather than left to chance, and each harness re-checks siteurl before touching anything.
nodes.norm_label: mysql socket pinned to arpcxvfuz to avoid cross-site pairing

nodes.label: --web mode runs suites through php-fpm instead of CLI PHP
nodes.rationale: CLI PHP on this machine has no Imagick, so a CLI-only run would silently exercise cwebp regardless of the engine requested. Web mode issues a token-authenticated request to web-runner.php so the suite runs under the site's actual PHP-FPM extensions.
nodes.norm_label: --web mode runs suites through php-fpm instead of cli php

nodes.label: Hard rule: never global $wpdb in plugin code
nodes.rationale: DB access must go through app/Models/ (OptimizationLog, UrlLookup). The two deliberate exceptions, DatabaseRewriter and DataBackfills, need serialization-safe multi-table SQL that cannot go through a model.
nodes.norm_label: hard rule: never global $wpdb in plugin code

nodes.label: Hard rule: never delete by glob over a shared directory
nodes.rationale: Delete only paths you created, resolved from your own records. A glob cleanup already destroyed 54 real user backups.
nodes.norm_label: hard rule: never delete by glob over a shared directory

nodes.label: Hard rule: never weaken a guard to make a test pass
nodes.rationale: Applies to is_serialized(), the __PHP_Incomplete_Class check, and the path-traversal check in BackupManager. If a guard blocks a test, the test is wrong, not the guard.
nodes.norm_label: hard rule: never weaken a guard to make a test pass

nodes.label: Hard rule: @wordpress/components is banned
nodes.rationale: The runtime (React, HTTP, i18n) comes from WordPress via @wordpress/element, @wordpress/api-fetch, @wordpress/i18n, externalized by wp-scripts. The UI does not: every control is the plugin's own, using sio-* classes, never core's notice/button/.description markup. build/admin.asset.php must list wp-element and wp-api-fetch but never wp-components.

nodes.label: Hard rule: never add a Composer runtime dependency
nodes.rationale: The plugin ships dependency-free by design; vendor/ holds only the generated autoloader. npm packages are build-time only and must still be named in the spec.
nodes.norm_label: hard rule: never add a composer runtime dependency

nodes.label: WPCS lives outside the plugin
nodes.rationale: npm run lint:php is used instead of require-dev'ing phpcs, because the committed vendor/ must stay autoloader-only (invariant 12). See context/specs/done/09-phpcs-compliance.md.

nodes.label: Hard rule: every input handler needs capability check, nonce, sanitize on input, escape on output
nodes.rationale: This is the plugin's real attack surface: REST routes, upload MIME handling, generated WebP paths, the cwebp shell-out, backup/restore file paths, unserialize in Services/Rewrite/.
nodes.norm_label: hard rule: every input handler needs capability check, nonce, sanitize on input, escape on output

nodes.label: Hard rule: never hand-edit build/**
nodes.rationale: build/** is wp-scripts output; edit resources/** and run npm run build instead.

nodes.label: Hard rule: never touch wp-content/uploads/swift-image-optimizer/backup/
nodes.rationale: That directory is user data, often the only copy of the original image.

nodes.label: FluentCart-style layout (app/ + framework/ roots)
nodes.rationale: No src/, Providers/, Repositories/, Foundation/ inside app/, and no Http/Admin/. The kernel lives at its own framework/ root outside app/, mirroring how FluentCart keeps FluentCart\Framework\* outside app/.

nodes.label: Core premise: this plugin rewrites and deletes user media, backup is often the only copy
nodes.rationale: A bug here does not produce a broken page, it produces a media library the user cannot get back. This drives every hard rule in the file.
nodes.norm_label: core premise: this plugin rewrites and deletes user media, backup is often the only copy

nodes.label: Invariant 22: a column describing a file is not evidence the file exists — ask the disk
nodes.rationale: BackupManager::manifest_is_intact() before offering Restore, AttachmentConverter::optimized_output_exists() before reporting or refusing an optimization. The database and uploads directory can be restored from different points in time. Trusting the column showed a whole library as processed with no way to optimize any of it, and offered Restores that could not succeed. Three of Unit 11's four reports were this same mistake.
nodes.norm_label: invariant 22: a column describing a file is not evidence the file exists — ask the disk

nodes.label: Invariant 23: a batch persists its pending rewrite map before applying it
nodes.rationale: Runner parks pending_rewrite, rewrites, then clears it; the next batch flushes anything left behind. Conversion writes a terminal log row per image but repoints references once per batch; a death in between leaves those images marked done forever with references pointing at filenames that no longer exist, and Scanner never revisits a terminal row. Tolerable when a batch was one foreground request; not once cron runs batches unattended.
nodes.norm_label: invariant 23: a batch persists its pending rewrite map before applying it

nodes.label: Invariant 24: the server owns whether a bulk run is active
nodes.rationale: start() is idempotent, cancel() keeps the cursor, and the client reconciles from state() rather than computing its own. Two clients doing their own arithmetic over different snapshots is why progress figures disagreed, and an unguarded start() let a second tab reset a run mid-flight, surfacing as 'already running' from a button that looked available.
nodes.norm_label: invariant 24: the server owns whether a bulk run is active

nodes.label: framework/ kernel root, outside app/
nodes.rationale: Reproduces the ~1,200 lines of wpfluent/framework the plugin actually uses (container, config, view, router); not installable via Composer because the wpfluent GitHub org is private and absent from Packagist.

nodes.label: Feature 1: auto-optimize on upload
nodes.rationale: Runs in wp_handle_upload, after the file is moved into uploads/ but before wp_insert_attachment, so WordPress creates the attachment as native .webp and generates every subsize as WebP itself. Consequence: zero URL rewriting needed.

nodes.label: Feature 2: individual / bulk optimization
nodes.rationale: Retro-fits images already in the Media Library that have references scattered across posts, meta and options; needs URL rewriting, which is why AttachmentConverter plus Rewrite/ is ten times the size of Upload/Interceptor.php.

nodes.label: Decision: no AVIF, WebP only
nodes.rationale: AVIF encoding is 5-10x slower, punishing across a large library. Tracked in future-specs/avif-support.md.

nodes.label: Decision: no client-side conversion
nodes.rationale: Cimo's canvas.toBlob approach is fast but breaks in Safari, needs an open browser tab, and cannot do bulk without downloading and re-uploading every image.

nodes.label: Decision: no external HTTP requests of any kind
nodes.rationale: No telemetry, no phone-home, no licence check.
nodes.norm_label: decision: no external http requests of any kind

nodes.label: Decision: no non-destructive mode
nodes.rationale: Originals are replaced and URLs rewritten by explicit product decision; the safety net is backups + retention + restore, not a parallel-file mode.

nodes.label: Tech constraints: PHP 7.4+, WP 6.2+, no Composer runtime dep
nodes.rationale: Verified: every file parses under PHP 7.4, 8.2 and 8.4. WP 6.2 minimum because the admin bundle uses createRoot from @wordpress/element (React 18). @wordpress/scripts is a dev dependency only.
nodes.norm_label: tech constraints: php 7.4+, wp 6.2+, no composer runtime dep
